properties.name: DEFECT (flo2, 2026-09-14, twice in one day): approving a node you authored ERASES the record that you authored it — AUTHORED_BY is keyed without its role, and the setter reports what it wrote, not what it displaced
properties.statement:
REPORTED by flo2, relayed by Anthony 2026-09-14, in flo2's words: "The compare_designs pass before opening this PR caught that setting approver had overwritten the author edges on two rules — the graph had stopped saying you wrote them in August. Restored, with the approver signature moved to the decision that governs all three. That's the second time today the same mechanism bit: AUTHORED_BY holds one edge per contributor per node, so a node you both write and later settle loses its authorship to the settling call, silently, because the setter reports what it wrote and not what it displaced. It was caught only because the PR body is built from compare_designs — the rule that made the loss visible is one of the rules that lost its author."

═══ THE MECHANISM, CONFIRMED IN CODE ═══
`foundation/store/keys.rs::edge_key(graph_id, edge_type, from_id, to_id)` — the ROLE is not part of the key. `graph.rs::authored_by` calls `create_edge` with `role` and `acted_at` as PROPERTIES. So a second AUTHORED_BY from the same node to the same Contributor is the SAME key, and the write replaces the first edge's properties wholesale: `role=author` becomes `role=approver`, and `acted_at` moves too. Every path that sets an approver — `set_requirement_status`/`set_decision_status` with `approver`, the constructors' `status`+`approver`, `acknowledge_*` with an approver — goes through this. Nothing reports the displacement: the setter returns the edge it wrote.

═══ MEASURED ON REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN ═══
842 (node, contributor) AUTHORED_BY pairs. Pairs carrying BOTH `author` and `approver`: ZERO — which is not a fact about practice, it is impossible by construction. Pairs carrying `approver` only: 389 (Decision 325, Requirement 42, DesignRule 15, ChangeEvent 6, Capability 1). How many of those 389 were once `author` edges cannot be read from the export — the displacement leaves no trace, which is the defect. INFERENCE, stated as such: reflow2's design is authored almost entirely by one person, who also approves, so most of the 325 approver-only Decisions were very likely author edges that the accepting call overwrote. Not a measurement; a reason to think the count is large rather than small.

═══ WHY IT IS A DEFECT AND NOT A MODELLING CHOICE ═══
`dec:design-authorship-identity` says AUTHORED_BY "is past tense and never changes" (graph.rs, nodes.rs). The approver write changes it. `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` made the approver signature load-bearing — `check_intent_authority` gates CI on it — and the SAME write that adds the signature the gate reads removes the authorship the design promised was permanent. Two designs (flo2 and, by inference, this one) have lost August authorship to September rulings, and only a diff-based PR body noticed.

═══ TWO FIX SHAPES, not chosen ═══
(a) AT THE CAUSE: an author and an approver are two facts, so they must be two edges — put the role in what makes an AUTHORED_BY edge distinct, or hold roles as a set on one edge. Then approving cannot displace authoring. ⚠️ Touches the edge key or the edge shape: an export/import migration and every reader of `role` (report.rs walks it in at least three places).
(b) THE PATCH THAT MAKES IT LOUD: flo2's proposal — the setters report a displaced role the way prose_currency reports stale prose ("this write replaced role=author acted_at=2026-08-04 on this edge"). ⚠️ Anthony's standing rule is to fix at the root, and (b) alone leaves every past displacement unrecoverable and every future one merely announced.
The honest order is (a), with (b)'s reporting kept for the case where a write DOES intend to change a role.

═══ WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED ═══
The count of already-displaced edges on either design. flo2 restored two by hand from compare_designs; nothing here can restore reflow2's own.
